supersedesCorrects.priorClaim: openspec/changes/parent-atlas-retrieval-lineage-dag-convergence/tasks.md's LEGACY-HASH-WRITER-IDENTIFICATION-01 (2026-09-15, earlier same day) stated codebase-semantic-indexer.ts writes 'content_hash: chunk.contentHash straight to the column' in codebase_chunk_index.
supersedesCorrects.correction: FALSE. Verified by reading the full file: codebase-semantic-indexer.ts contains zero Postgres references (no 'pg', 'Pool', 'INSERT INTO' anywhere in the file). Its content_hash write (line 677) is a QDRANT PAYLOAD field on a point later sent via upsertPoints() -- never a direct Postgres write. The underlying HASH FORMULA attribution (SHA-256 truncated to 16 hex chars, of one chunk's text) was correct; only the write-path description (direct vs Qdrant-mediated) was wrong.
supersedesCorrects.realMechanism: codebase-semantic-indexer.ts writes points into Qdrant collection 'codebase_chunks_768' with payload.content_hash = 16-char truncated SHA-256 of chunk text. A SEPARATE script, sveltekit-frontend/scripts/mirror-qdrant-to-postgres.ts, scrolls that SAME Qdrant collection ('codebase_chunks_768', confirmed matching default) and upserts payload.content_hash verbatim into Postgres codebase_chunk_index.content_hash (line ~338: textOrNull(payload.content_hash)). This is a two-hop pipeline, not a direct write.

confirmedWriters.mechanism: DIRECT Postgres write via real parameterized INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (qdrant_id) DO UPDATE

INDIRECT Postgres write: indexer writes SHA-256(chunk text).slice(0,16) into a Qdrant point payload (collection codebase_chunks_768); mirror script separately scrolls that collection and copies payload.content_hash verbatim into Postgres via INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (qdrant_id) DO UPDATE SET content_hash = EXCLUDED.content_hash

DIRECT Postgres write, gated: UPDATE codebase_chunk_index SET content_hash = $2 WHERE id = $1 AND content_hash IS NULL (only fills NULL rows, never overwrites an existing value; requires --apply flag)
confirmedWriters.formula: shortContentHash(text) = createHash('sha256').update(Buffer.from(text,'utf8')).digest('hex').slice(0, 16), computed over pgRow.content (the chunk row's own content column)
confirmedWriters.note: Uses the identical 16-char-truncated-chunk-SHA256 convention as the indexer/mirror pair above -- reinforces this is a systemic convention across 3 code paths, not an isolated mistake.

graphifyFilesWriterConfirmed.chain: sveltekit-frontend/scripts/atlas/observe-workspace-source-binding.mts (reads whole file via node:fs readFile) -> deriveCodeSourceRevisionV1() in sveltekit-frontend/src/lib/server/atlas/identity/code-source-revision-v1.ts -> sveltekit-frontend/scripts/atlas/materialize-graphify-source-inventory.mts (INSERT INTO graphify_files)
graphifyFilesWriterConfirmed.formula: createHash('sha256').update(Buffer.from(source, 'utf8')).digest('hex') -- full 64-char hex, NO truncation, computed over the ENTIRE file content read from disk
graphifyFilesWriterConfirmed.confirmsDesignAssumption: Confirms design.md's assumption that graphify_files/graphify_execution_file_membership_v2.content_hash is genuinely whole-file scoped, not merely observed-as-uniformly-64-char. No line-ending or other normalization is applied before hashing -- relevant to design.md's first Open Question.

scopeHonesty.looseReferenceUniverseSize: 150+ files reference 'codebase_chunk_index' across scripts/atlas and sveltekit-frontend/scripts for many unrelated reasons (embedding backfills, kmeans clustering, sparse encoding, phase-N summary pipelines, etc.)
scopeHonesty.mitigatingEvidence: 59 of those files were confirmed via grep to contain a real INSERT/UPDATE statement against the table; of those, only files also matching a tight content_hash-proximity filter (24 files) were individually read. The remaining ~35 write-capable files were not read this pass and are NOT classified -- they write other columns (embeddings, clusters, tags, summaries) per their filenames, but this is an inference from naming, not a confirmed read.
scopeHonesty.honestConclusion: WRITER_AUDIT_PARTIAL, not WRITER_AUDIT_COMPLETE. Both hash-length buckets (16-char and 64-char) now have confirmed, read-verified writers. A residual, unquantified risk remains that an unread file among the ~35 unclassified write-capable candidates writes content_hash using a third convention -- this cannot be ruled out from this pass alone.
